summary: Presents Operations, Administration, and Maintenance requirements for TRILL networks, covering the functions and tools needed to monitor and troubleshoot them. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A list of the checkup tools a network needs, so a repair person can see what is wrong and fix it.

subtitle: Diagnostic and monitoring requirements for TRILL campus networks.

tldr.problem: TRILL networks (data center switching fabrics) need operational tools to monitor health, check connectivity, trace paths, and measure performance. Without standards, each vendor implements diagnostics differently.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a set of OAM (Operations, Administration, and Maintenance) functions that TRILL equipment must support: connectivity checks, path tracing, performance monitoring, fault detection, and continuity checks between routing bridges.
tldr.outcome: Network operators gain a unified framework to troubleshoot TRILL deployments, verify that traffic follows expected paths, detect failures quickly, and measure latency and packet loss.

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: OAM between Routing Bridges (RBridges) within a TRILL campus

facts.label: Core functions
facts.value: 5: connectivity, continuity, path tracing, performance, fault detection

today: RFC 6905 is Informational. It has guided the development of TRILL OAM protocol specifications and remains the reference for TRILL diagnostic requirements. Actual protocol implementations (such as those in TRILL switches and monitoring platforms) build on these requirements.

sections.title: TRILL and the Need for Operational Tools
sections.content:
TRILL (Transparent Interconnection of Lots of Links) is a protocol for high-speed data center switching that routes across a mesh of switches called a campus. Managing and troubleshooting a large TRILL campus requires operational tools.

The RFC defines OAM requirements—the functions and capabilities that TRILL equipment must provide. OAM covers five areas: verifying connectivity between switches, continuously checking liveliness, tracing the path a packet takes through the network, measuring performance metrics, and alerting operators to faults and defects. These tools are vital for wider adoption of TRILL in large data centers.
sections.eli5: TRILL is a way for data center switches to talk to each other. OAM is the set of diagnostic tools operators use to make sure everything is working and to find problems when they occur.

sections.title: Connectivity and Continuity Checks
sections.content:
Two core OAM functions verify that switches can reach each other. Connectivity verification tests whether one switch can send and receive packets from another, either over any available path or over a specific path taken by a particular flow of traffic. Continuity checks are periodic, ongoing liveliness tests: one switch sends probes to another at intervals and raises an alarm if replies stop arriving for too long.

Both functions must work for unicast paths (between two switches) and for distribution trees (one-to-many multicast). The RFC requires that OAM can verify both the full tree and the pruned tree (the portion actually in use by a particular flow).
sections.eli5: Connectivity check: 'Can switch A talk to switch B?' Continuity check: 'Is switch B still alive?' Both need to work for different types of traffic paths.

sections.title: Path Tracing and Performance Monitoring
sections.content:
Path tracing (like the traceroute command) shows all the switches a packet traverses from source to destination. For TRILL, this must work for specific unicast flows and for multicast distribution trees. The RFC recommends support for tracing all available least-cost paths, not just one.

Performance monitoring measures two key metrics: packet loss (how many packets fail to reach the destination) and packet delay (how long packets take to arrive). The RFC requires measurement of two-way delay (round-trip time) and optionally one-way delay. Loss and delay can be measured end-to-end, over a section of the path, or across all equal-cost paths.
sections.eli5: Path tracing: 'What route does my packet take?' Performance monitoring: 'How many packets get lost?' and 'How long do they take to arrive?'

sections.title: The OAM Framework
sections.content:
The RFC requires a single unified OAM framework covering all TRILL functions. This framework must be extensible (using version numbers and TLV structures) and should reuse concepts from existing OAM standards such as Ethernet OAM (IEEE 802.1ag) and MPLS OAM standards.

OAM functions must be able to run concurrently without interfering with each other. For example, a proactive continuity check can run at the same time as an operator manually testing connectivity. Operators must be able to initiate checks on demand or run them proactively at regular intervals. All errors and results must be logged and accessible via SNMP.
sections.eli5: All OAM tools use the same basic framework, can be extended with new features, and work together without getting in each other's way.

sections.title: Security and Fault Notification
sections.content:
OAM messages must not be misused for denial-of-service attacks or to gather sensitive network topology information from unauthorized users. Rate limiting and shaping must be available to prevent OAM from causing congestion. OAM packets must remain within the TRILL campus and never leak out to the wider network.

The RFC requires a Fault Indication framework to notify the ingress switch (or syslog servers) when connectivity fails. It also recommends a Defect Indication framework to detect prolonged service interruptions, with configurable thresholds, logging, and optional remote notification to the originating switch. The system should support both in-band (within TRILL) and out-of-band (external) notification modes.
sections.eli5: Keep OAM secure by limiting who can use it and what they can learn. When something breaks, alert the right people, either inside the network or externally.

items.title: Connectivity Check
items.text: Test if two switches can reach each other over any path or a specific flow path.

items.title: Continuity Check
items.text: Periodically verify that a switch remains alive and reachable.

items.title: Path Tracing
items.text: Show the sequence of switches a packet traverses from source to destination.

items.title: Performance Metrics
items.text: Measure packet loss and round-trip delay over the TRILL path.
